back: The commercial centre of a town: main shops, offices, banks; highest land values and buildings; few residents.
Edge-of-town zone mixing rural and urban uses: smallholdings, new housing, malls, cemeteries, sewage works.
Number of houses or people per unit area: high density = small plots, low density = large plots.
Rings round the CBD: transition zone, low-income, medium-income, high-income commuter zone.
Wedges along transport routes: industry with low-income housing; high-income sector extending away from industry.
A town grows round several centres: CBD, outlying business districts, industrial districts, suburban centres.
Industry south and south-west along the railway (Workington, Southerton) and east (Msasa); high-density suburbs south and west; low-density north and north-east.

front: Why African towns differ from the models
back: Colonial racial planning, relief and wetlands, informal settlements, satellite towns; models were based on US cities.
